findings.title: The well-formed ledger scenario still describes the goal by its bare prefix `**G1`
findings.recommendation: The walk made goal IDs match whole: a goal ID must be followed by a space, an em dash or `**`, so `G1` never matches `G10`. But the ADDED scenario `A well-formed ledger entry writes` still sets its precondition as 'the doc holds `**G1` under `## Goals`', which is the prefix form the walk retired. A test written to this scenario may build a fixture of just `**G1` with nothing after it, which the whole-ID rule refuses, so the scenario and the rule disagree. Restate the precondition as 'the doc holds `**G1 — …**` under `## Goals`', the form `automate-dev-flow.md` actually uses (line 35).

findings.title: The archived-change lookup reads two ways when a change name was archived more than once
findings.recommendation: The lookup says to try the archived change's `decisions/` folder 'taking the lexically greatest when several match; the first folder holding `resolution-<token>.json` is used'. With two archived directories for one name (a name reused after an archive), one implementer takes only the newest directory and refuses a citation whose record sits in the older one; another searches every matching directory. Settle it in one sentence: search the matching archived directories newest first, and use the first one that holds the file. That is the reading consistent with 'the first folder holding' and with precedent from any earlier change. Design Decision 5 should say the same.
